questions.q: A specific indirect tax shifts the supply curve:
opts: Upwards (to the left) by the amount of the tax
Downwards (to the right) by the amount of the tax
questions.fb: A tax raises firms' costs by a fixed amount per unit, so the supply curve shifts up (left) by the amount of the tax. See section 1 in the Learn tab.
questions.model: Upwards (to the left) by the amount of the tax

questions.q: A $5 per unit tax is placed on a good and 200 units are sold. How much revenue does the government raise ($)?
questions.fb: Revenue = tax per unit × quantity sold = 5 × 200 = 1,000. See section 1.

questions.q: If demand for a taxed good is inelastic, consumers are likely to:
opts: Bear most of the tax burden
Bear very little of the burden
questions.fb: The less elastic side pays more. Inelastic demand means consumers cannot easily cut back, so they bear most of the burden and the tax barely reduces consumption. See 'Incidence' in section 1.
questions.model: Bear most of the tax burden

questions.q: What does a per-unit subsidy to producers do to the market?
opts: Lowers the price and raises quantity
Raises the price and lowers quantity
questions.fb: A subsidy lowers costs, so supply shifts right: price falls and quantity rises. See section 2.
questions.model: Lowers the price and raises quantity

questions.q: The government pays a $3 per unit subsidy and 400 units are sold. What is the cost to the government ($)?
questions.fb: Cost = subsidy per unit × quantity = 3 × 400 = 1,200. See section 2.

questions.q: For a maximum price to have any effect it must be set:
questions.fb: A price ceiling only bites if it is below the equilibrium price; above it, it has no effect. See section 4.

questions.q: Complete: a maximum price set below equilibrium creates a ________.
questions.fb: At the lower price quantity demanded rises and quantity supplied falls, creating a shortage. See section 4.

questions.q: Complete: a minimum price set above equilibrium creates a ________.
questions.fb: At the higher price quantity supplied rises and quantity demanded falls, creating a surplus. See section 5.

questions.q: In a buffer stock scheme, what does the agency do when the price would fall below the minimum?
questions.fb: To defend the minimum price it buys up the surplus and stores it. When the price would rise above the maximum, it sells from stock. See section 6.

questions.q: Which is a typical limitation of using indirect taxes on goods with inelastic demand?
questions.fb: With inelastic demand the tax raises revenue but does little to reduce consumption, so it may not achieve the aim of reducing demerit goods. See 'Limits' in section 1.
